guarantees.claim: out is continuously driven as the concatenation of ctrl_we, alert, data_in_we, ~data_out_we, data_in_prev_sel, ~data_in_prev_we, state_in_sel, add_state_in_sel, add_state_out_sel, ~ctr_incr, ~cipher_in_valid, ~cipher_out_ready, ~cipher_crypt_out_buf, ~cipher_dec_key_gen_out_buf, cipher_prng_reseed_out_buf, cipher_key_clear_out_buf, cipher_data_out_clear_out_buf, key_init_sel, ~key_init_we, iv_sel, ~iv_we, prng_data_req, prng_reseed_req, start_we, key_iv_data_in_clear_we, data_out_clear_we, prng_reseed_out_buf, prng_reseed_we, idle, idle_we, stall, stall_we, output_lost_out_buf, output_lost_we, output_valid, output_valid_we, input_ready, input_ready_we.

uncertain_points.claim: Several control/status signals (data_out_we, data_in_prev_we, ctr_incr, cipher_in_valid, cipher_out_ready, cipher_crypt_out_buf, cipher_dec_key_gen_out_buf, key_init_we, iv_we) are inverted before being packed into out. The design intent for the polarity of these bits on the out bus is not explicit, leaving ambiguity whether the consumer expects active-high or active-low behavior.
uncertain_points.cond: when out is used by downstream logic
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream interpretation mismatch could invert the meaning of these control signals, potentially causing incorrect data flow, timing, or security-critical operations (e.g., unintended enable/clear actions).
